newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up on some speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up on some speculative buying.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Friday as investors bought speculatively in some leading stocks, brokers said.
They added the market would likely remain broadly stable early next week.
Friday, the General Index rose 0.3 percent to 1,530.1 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.8 percent to 2,209.1 points.
In a total of 1,544 trades, volume was estimated at 64.6 million soles ($24.9 million), brokers said, adding the inflated volume was due to cross-trades in second-tier stocks.
Brokers said Friday's trade saw small swings throughout the day.

"The movement was basically speculative, which was shown by the quick changes in investor behavior and the variation in the main indices," said an analyst at a leading local brokerage, who asked not to be named.
Losing some of the ground it gained Thursday, benchmark Telefnica del Per fell 0.7 percent, closing at 5.71 soles on volume of 1.7 million shares.
Among other leaders, most interest was shown in Backus y Johnston. The country's largest brewery rose 1.4 percent to 2.18 soles in volume of 1.8 million shares.
Chocolate maker D'Onofrio DON.LM rose 8.18 percent to 1.19 soles on volume of 210,000 after rumors of a possible joint venture with a foreign company resurfaced, brokers said.
